column2: Maya wants permanent coverage despite a recent diagnosis. Which feature of her term policy could she use?
column7: Conversion lets Maya switch to permanent insurance during the conversion window without fresh medical underwriting. Renewal extends the term coverage.

column2: A variable annuity's stock subaccount loses value. Who bears that loss without a guarantee?
column7: The owner bears the market risk on the selected subaccount investments.

column2: A beneficiary chooses ten years of installments and lets the insurer calculate each payment. Which settlement option fits?
column7: A fixed period sets the duration. With a fixed amount, the beneficiary chooses each payment's size and the balance determines how long payments last.

column2: Which rider lets a terminally ill insured draw against the policy's face amount while alive?
column7: This rider advances some or all of the death benefit for a qualifying illness. A waiver covers premiums during a qualifying disability.

column2: A consumer report helps a life insurer decide to charge an applicant more. Which notice does that trigger?
column7: The Fair Credit Reporting Act requires an adverse action notice when a consumer report contributes to a higher rate, even if other factors carry more weight.

column2: Ana receives a $60,000 death benefit plus $900 interest. How much generally enters her federal gross income?
column7: The $60,000 paid because of the insured's death is generally excluded from federal gross income. The $900 interest is taxable.

column2: To hurt a rival's business, a Texas agent falsely tells customers the rival insurer is insolvent. Which violation fits?
column7: The agent deliberately spreads a false claim about the rival insurer's financial condition to damage its business. Texas law treats this as defamation.

column2: After her Texas license expires, Liv solicits a new sale ($90 commission). Earlier licensed sales also renew ($210). What may she collect?
column7: Texas permits renewal commissions on sales Liv made while licensed. She cannot collect a commission for soliciting a sale after her license expired.

column2: Which document gives a life insurer permission to write specified lines of insurance in Texas?
column7: The insurer's certificate of authority identifies which lines of insurance it may transact in Texas.

column2: A Texas policy lists age 44. The premium buys $90,000 at 44 and $70,000 at the insured's actual age, 49. What death benefit is payable?
column7: With age understated, Texas uses the coverage the premium would have bought at the insured's actual age. Here that is $70,000.

column2: A parent needs the same death benefit until her child turns 18. Which temporary coverage fits?
column7: Level term keeps the face amount constant throughout the chosen period. Decreasing term provides less coverage as time passes.

column2: A homeowner wants life coverage to shrink as a mortgage is repaid. Which policy fits?
column7: Under decreasing term insurance, the death benefit falls according to a schedule. That schedule can be chosen to match a declining debt.

column2: Jo bought annually renewable term at 43. What age generally sets her next year's premium?
column7: Term renewals generally use the insured's attained age. A one-year term bought at 43 renews at 44.

column2: A nonrenewable term policy expires tomorrow. How can its owner obtain another term of coverage?
column7: A nonrenewable policy ends when its term expires. The owner must qualify for a new policy to obtain further term coverage.

column2: Who receives the face amount if an ordinary term policy expires while the insured is alive?
column7: Ordinary term insurance pays the face amount for death during the insured period. Surviving to expiration does not trigger that benefit.

column2: What does return-of-premium term insurance pay at its stated refund date if the insured survives?
column7: The contract identifies the premiums eligible for refund. The face amount is the benefit for a covered death.

column2: Which policy builds guaranteed cash value with level premiums scheduled throughout the insured's life?
column7: Ordinary whole life spreads scheduled level premiums over the insured's lifetime. Twenty-payment life finishes the premium schedule sooner.

column2: At age 50, Rosa finishes paying for her 20-pay whole life policy. What happens next?
column7: Twenty-pay describes the premium schedule. Once Rosa completes it, the whole life policy is paid up.

column2: For identical coverage, why are annual premiums usually higher on ten-pay life than ordinary life?
column7: Ten-pay life compresses the funding of lifetime coverage into ten premium years. Ordinary life spreads the payments over a longer period.

column2: A buyer wants lifetime protection fully funded at issue. Which contract meets that goal?
column7: A single payment at issue funds the policy. Other whole life payment schedules leave future premiums due.

column2: What helps pay later insurance costs when ordinary whole life's annual premium stays level?
column7: In the early years, premiums exceed the current cost of protection. The insurer invests the excess to help cover higher costs in later years.

column2: A universal life premium falls short of monthly charges. Where can the insurer take the difference?
column7: The insurer deducts charges from the policy's available cash value. Continuing to underfund the policy can exhaust that value.

column2: A universal life report projects lapse before maturity. Which change can help sustain the same coverage?
column7: Additional funding can cover insurance costs and keep the policy in force longer. A withdrawal depletes funds available for charges.

column2: Which feature can preserve universal life coverage at low account values if specified payments are met?
column7: A no-lapse guarantee maintains coverage under its stated funding and timing conditions. An interest-rate guarantee governs earnings on money in the account.

column2: Which policy lets its owner vary premiums and allocate cash value among stock and bond subaccounts?
column7: Variable universal life combines flexible funding with investment choices. Fixed-premium variable life also offers investment choices but prescribes the premium.

column2: What determines investment gains or losses on the cash value in a fixed-premium variable life subaccount?
column4: Change in the insurer's general surplus
column6: Change in an external stock index
column7: Variable life subaccount values follow the investments held in that subaccount. A fixed premium governs what the owner pays, not the investment return.

column2: How does indexed life insurance use an external stock benchmark when crediting a policy account?
column3: Applies a formula to index changes
column4: Pays the dividends on shares held
column5: Buys fund units for the insured
column6: Credits a fixed share of premiums
column7: The contract specifies how changes in its index translate into interest credits. The owner does not hold the index stocks through the policy.

column2: A current-assumption whole life policy promises a minimum crediting rate. What does that minimum protect?
column7: The interest-sensitive account accumulates premiums, less charges, at no less than the specified rate. The guarantee concerns credited interest.

column2: Two partners want one policy to fund a buyout while the surviving partner still runs the firm. Which contract fits?
column6: Single life on the senior partner
column7: A first-to-die policy can fund the buyout when either insured partner dies. A survivorship policy pays after the surviving partner also dies.

column2: Parents want one policy to fund a trust when both have died. Which coverage fits?
column6: Individual whole life on the younger
column7: Survivorship insurance covers both parents and pays on the last death. Either single-life policy could pay while the other parent is still living.

column2: A freelancer wants to contribute different sums to an annuity whenever income arrives. Which funding arrangement fits?
column7: A flexible-premium contract permits contributions to vary in size and timing within its terms. A fixed schedule requires specified payments.

column2: At 55, Gil deposits one lump sum for income starting at 70. What are the annuity's funding and timing?
column7: One contribution makes the contract single-premium. The fifteen-year wait for income makes it deferred.

column2: Nia buys an immediate annuity today. When must the insurer begin paying her income?
column7: An immediate annuity starts income within one year of purchase. The contract sets the first payment date within that window.

column2: Pat's deferred annuity earns interest while she is still making deposits. Which phase is underway?
column7: During accumulation, contributions and credited earnings build the contract's value. Income payments come during the payout phase.

column2: What happens when a retiree annuitizes the accumulated value of a deferred contract?
column7: Annuitization converts contract value into payments under the selected income option. The payment pattern depends on that option.

column2: Two spouses want annuity income to continue as long as either is alive. Which payout fits?
column7: Joint and survivor payments continue while either covered person lives. A period-certain guarantee ends after the stated period.

column2: A life annuity guarantees 12 years of payments. The annuitant dies after five. What does the beneficiary receive?
column7: The twelve-year guarantee starts with the annuity payments. Five years have passed, leaving seven years payable to the beneficiary.

column2: An annuitant dies shortly after choosing a straight life payout. What income goes to the heirs?
column7: A straight life payout lasts for the annuitant's lifetime. A refund or guaranteed payment period would require a different option.

column2: A fixed annuity guarantees 3% interest. The insurer earns 2% on its assets. Which rate is it bound to credit at minimum?
column7: The insurer backs the contractual interest floor. Its own investment return does not reduce its obligation below 3%.

column2: An annuity credits index gains up to 6% with full participation. What does an 11% gain earn?
column7: Full participation takes the entire index increase into account, but the cap limits the credit to 6%.

column2: An uncapped annuity credits half the index gain with no spread. What does an 8% increase earn?
column7: The participation rate is the share of the gain credited. Half of 8% is 4%.

column2: What supports a variable annuity's guaranteed death benefit if its investment subaccounts fall sharply?
column7: The insurer's ability to meet its obligations backs the guarantee. The underlying investments determine the market value of the subaccounts.

column2: Where can a buyer compare a variable annuity contract's expenses, risks and optional benefit charges?
column7: The prospectus describes the contract, its risks and its expenses. Each investment fund has its own prospectus as well.

column2: A deferred annuity owner withdraws more than the free allowance in year two. Which contract fee may apply?
column7: An early withdrawal beyond the contract's allowance can trigger a surrender charge on the excess. The charge schedule appears in the contract.

column2: A roofer qualifies for a disability waiver on his whole life policy. Which expense will the insurer absorb?
column7: A premium waiver keeps the required life premiums from coming due during a qualifying disability. It does not replace wages.

column2: A universal life rider waives monthly deductions during total disability. What stops during the waiver?
column7: The rider waives specified insurance and expense charges normally deducted from the account. Investment performance remains separate.

column2: A grandmother paying for her grandson's life policy dies. Which rider can keep his premiums paid?
column7: A payor benefit can waive premiums on a child's coverage after the covered payor dies. The child remains the insured.

column2: Which rider allows additional life coverage on specified dates even after the insured develops diabetes?
column7: Guaranteed insurability gives the owner scheduled opportunities to buy more coverage without new evidence of health. Additional premiums still apply.

column2: A policy has an accidental death rider. The insured recovers from a fracture, then dies of unrelated pneumonia. Which benefits apply?
column7: The rider requires death caused by a covered accident. An unrelated illness triggers the ordinary death benefit alone.

column2: Which optional benefit on a life policy can reimburse qualifying nursing facility expenses?
column7: A long-term care rider can cover eligible care costs according to its terms. Disability income replaces income rather than reimbursing a care bill.

column2: Emil has $80,000 whole life with a $40,000 term rider. What coverage remains when the rider expires?
column7: The temporary addition ends at expiration. The $80,000 base policy continues if it remains in force.

column2: Two siblings share a children's term rider. The older ages out. What happens to the still-eligible sibling?
column6: Loses coverage with the older child
column7: The rider insures each eligible child for its specified amount. One child's reaching the age limit does not change the younger child's benefit.

column2: Which rider can increase a policy's face amount as consumer prices rise?
column7: A cost-of-living rider ties coverage increases to an inflation measure specified in the contract, subject to the rider's limits.

column2: Which clause tells an owner whether the attached application forms part of the policy?
column7: The entire contract clause identifies the documents that make up the agreement. An application forms part of it when included as the clause provides.

column2: Rae names Luis primary, Kim first contingent and Jay second contingent. Luis dies before Rae. Who receives the proceeds?
column7: The surviving first contingent beneficiary takes the proceeds after the only primary beneficiary predeceases the insured. Jay would receive them if Kim also predeceased Rae.

column2: Which clause contains the carrier's promise to pay a benefit upon proof of a covered death?
column7: The insuring clause states the insurer's obligation to pay when a covered loss occurs and the contract's proof requirements are met.

column2: Elena wants to replace her policy's irrevocable beneficiary. Whose consent must she obtain?
column7: The current irrevocable beneficiary must agree before Elena can remove that designation. Naming a successor does not supply consent.

column2: Which designation includes the insured's present and future grandchildren without naming each recipient?
column7: A class designation identifies recipients through a stated relationship. The contract can include everyone who meets that description.

column2: A parent wants proceeds managed for a seven-year-old under written trust instructions. Whom should the policy name?
column7: Naming the trustee in that capacity directs the proceeds to the trust for the child. Naming the child personally does not give the trustee control.

column2: Why might twelve monthly payments cost more than one annual payment on the same life policy?
column7: An insurer may use a modal factor to calculate installment premiums. The annual total can then vary with the payment schedule even when coverage and risk class stay the same.

column2: An owner elects automatic premium loans. How is an overdue premium funded while enough loan value remains?
column7: The insurer advances the premium as a loan secured by the policy. The missed payment creates a debt rather than a premium waiver.

column2: Which request may require fresh health evidence and overdue premiums to restore a lapsed policy?
column7: Reinstatement restores the original coverage after lapse. The insurer may ask for evidence of insurability and overdue premiums with interest.

column2: A $95,000 life benefit has $7,000 of unpaid policy debt including interest. What proceeds remain?
column7: The insurer deducts outstanding policy debt from the death benefit. Subtracting $7,000 from $95,000 leaves $88,000.

column2: An owner wants part of her universal life cash value without borrowing. Which transaction fits?
column7: A partial surrender removes part of the cash value. It does not create a loan balance and can reduce the death benefit.

column2: A whole life owner stops paying premiums but wants smaller lifelong coverage. Which nonforfeiture option fits?
column7: The cash value buys a smaller permanent policy requiring no further premiums. Extended term keeps protection for a limited time.

column2: An owner without policy debt chooses extended term insurance. What determines how long the original face amount continues?
column3: Term the cash value can buy
column7: Available cash value buys a term of insurance at the original face amount. The resulting term can be shorter than the original coverage period.

column2: A policy has $13,000 cash value, a $900 surrender charge and no debt. What does full surrender pay?
column7: The insurer deducts the applicable surrender charge from cash value. The payment is $13,000 less $900, and coverage ends.

column2: A participating whole life illustration shows a dividend next year. What amount can the owner count on?
column7: Participating dividends depend on the insurer's experience. An illustrated amount does not commit the insurer to declaring it.

column2: How can an owner use this year's dividend to increase permanent coverage without ongoing extra premiums?
column7: Paid-up additions buy extra whole life coverage with the dividend. Leaving funds on deposit accumulates money with the insurer.

column2: Leila wants her dividends to build a cash fund with the insurer without buying additional coverage. Which election fits?
column7: The accumulation option leaves declared dividends with the insurer to earn interest. Paid-up additions and one-year term use dividends to buy more insurance.

column2: A lender holds a collateral assignment on a $100,000 policy securing $24,000 still owed. What is the lender's share?
column7: A collateral assignment gives the lender first claim up to the remaining secured debt. The balance of the proceeds goes to the beneficiary.

column2: Quinn makes an absolute assignment to his daughter. Who can now direct changes to the policy?
column7: An absolute assignment transfers ownership rights to the assignee. Quinn's daughter now controls the policy.

column2: Which settlement leaves the full death proceeds with the insurer and pays the beneficiary only their earnings?
column7: The insurer holds the principal and pays the interest it earns. Installment settlements can pay out principal as well.

column2: A beneficiary elects life income and outlives her projected life expectancy. When do payments end?
column7: Life income continues for the beneficiary's lifetime. A longer life can produce total payments greater than the original death benefit.

column2: A commercial diver discloses diabetes. Which risk may a term insurer specifically exclude under Insurance Compact standards?
column7: The standards allow a specific occupation exclusion based on underwriting. They prohibit a death benefit exclusion for a specific medical condition.

column2: An accident permanently costs an insured the sight of one eye. Which rider may pay a scheduled benefit?
column7: Dismemberment coverage can pay specified amounts for listed losses, including sight. The insured need not die for this benefit.

column2: Which provision limits the insurer's time to challenge a policy based on the original application?
column7: The incontestability provision restricts challenges after a stated period during the insured's lifetime. The grace period concerns overdue premiums.

column2: A flood kills the insured and her beneficiary. Neither death can be placed first. Which provision addresses the claim?
column7: A common disaster clause can supply an order of death when both people die in the same event and the actual sequence cannot be established. It may treat the insured as the survivor.

column2: Mila applies to own a policy on her adult sister. Which two people sign as principals?
column7: The proposed owner and the adult whose life will be insured each sign in their own capacity. An agent who witnesses the signatures cannot sign for either sister.

column2: The owner accepts a home-office cut to the requested face amount. Whose written consent is also required?
column7: Under the Insurance Compact application standard, a change in the amount of insurance requires written consent from both the owner and the proposed insured.

column2: An applicant supplies a missing answer by phone. When must she receive the completed written application?
column3: Before she is asked to sign
column7: Texas requires the insurer to give the applicant the complete written application, including verbal answers, before asking her to sign and submit it.

column2: What does an applicant affirm by making a representation about her medical history?
column3: Her answers reflect what she knows and believes
column4: Her answers bind the insurer to issue coverage
column5: Her answers guarantee each fact is exact
column6: Her answers take the place of medical records
column7: A representation states what the applicant believes to be true. A warranty would promise strict accuracy. The distinction does not excuse a knowingly false answer.

column2: An applicant pays with the application. What determines whether temporary coverage exists during underwriting?
column6: Date of the first agent interview
column7: A conditional receipt may provide temporary insurance if its requirements are met. Paying the first premium alone does not settle whether those requirements were satisfied.

column2: When can a family cancel its old life policy without creating a gap during replacement?
column3: Once the new coverage is in force
column4: Once the new application is signed
column5: When the medical exam is complete
column6: When the new premium is quoted
column7: An application can still be declined or offered on different terms. Keeping the old policy in force until the new protection starts preserves continuous coverage.

column2: Before an HIV test for a Texas life application, what must the proposed insured ordinarily provide?
column7: Texas requires disclosure of the HIV test and written authorization on a separate consent form. Consent to a routine examination does not authorize that test.

column2: Mara revokes permission for her clinic to share records with a life insurer. When does her written revocation take effect?
column5: When the life insurer receives it
column6: When the doctor updates her chart
column7: Under HIPAA, the revocation takes effect when the covered entity authorized to disclose the records receives it. It does not undo an earlier authorized disclosure.

column2: Which product falls under FinCEN's insurance anti-money laundering rule for covered products?
column7: Individual permanent life insurance is covered because it can hold cash value. Ordinary group term, credit term and disability income coverage lack that investment feature.

column2: An annuity buyer shows little interest in investment returns. A strong focus on which feature raises a FinCEN red flag?
column7: FinCEN identifies intense interest in getting out of a contract combined with indifference to its investment performance as a warning sign. That combination warrants review.

column2: Who has the federal filing duty when a life agent flags a suspicious whole-life purchase?
column7: Under FinCEN's insurance rule, agents relay relevant information through the insurer's program. The insurer determines whether the transaction requires a suspicious activity report and files it when required.

column2: An insurer plans to share private data for an unrelated retailer's own advertising. When must it offer an opt-out?
column7: The insurer must give the customer an opportunity to opt out before first sharing the data. Waiting for the retailer to use the information is too late.

column2: An outside firm uses customer data to market an insurer's policies on the insurer's behalf. What agreement does GLBA require?
column3: Contract binding the firm to confidentiality
column4: Agreement to audit the firm annually
column6: Agreement to approve each mailing list
column7: The service-provider exception requires full disclosure of the information sharing and a contract requiring the firm to keep that information confidential.

column2: Which relationship gives a bank a financial interest in a particular person's continued life?
column3: An outstanding loan to that person
column4: An appointment to open an account
column5: A bid to lease that person's shop
column6: An invitation to sponsor a local event
column7: A creditor stands to lose money if its borrower dies before repayment. A prospective commercial relationship alone does not establish that particular loss.

column2: Investors recruit a retiree to buy a new policy for their benefit. Which arrangement does this describe?
column7: In stranger-originated life insurance, investors arrange for a policy to be issued for their benefit from the outset. A conventional life settlement involves selling a policy the owner already holds.

column2: An MIB entry conflicts with an applicant's answer about prior treatment. What should the underwriter do?
column6: Treat the entry as a diagnosis
column7: MIB information flags differences that need checking. A member insurer investigates before it makes an underwriting decision from the entry.

column2: An insurer denies coverage partly because of a consumer report. Who supplies the applicant's free copy on timely request?
column7: The Fair Credit Reporting Act gives the applicant a right to a free report from the reporting agency. The insurer identifies that agency in its adverse action notice.

column2: Which underwriting record best shows the course of a patient's treatment over several years?
column7: The treating physician's notes record diagnoses, observations and changes in treatment over time. A single exam or test shows findings at one point.

column2: Tariq qualifies for whole life coverage with an extra charge for elevated mortality. How did the insurer classify him?
column7: Underwriters may place an applicant with higher expected mortality in a substandard class and charge more. An applicant rated uninsurable would receive no offer.

column2: A carrier evaluates prescription and driving histories instead of ordering an exam. Which process fits?
column7: Accelerated underwriting can use outside data to evaluate risk without a physical examination. A guaranteed-issue offer does not depend on clearing this individualized risk assessment.

column2: A policy requires acceptance and initial payment. Luis accepts Monday and pays Wednesday. When does coverage begin?
column7: Assuming the other conditions are met and no temporary insurance applies, both acceptance and payment are required. Luis completes the last step on Wednesday.

column2: Before delivery, a hospitalization changes an answer on a pending application. Who should receive the update?
column4: The physician who did the exam
column7: Application agreements require changes in the applicant's answers to be reported to the insurer before delivery. The insurer decides whether the new information changes its offer.

column2: A life policy carries a flat extra rating. How does the insurer ordinarily calculate the charge?
column4: Dollar rate per $1,000 of cash value
column7: A flat extra applies a stated dollar rate to each unit of coverage. For a rate quoted per $1,000, the insurer divides the basic coverage amount by $1,000 and multiplies by the rate.

column2: An agent promises to waive a medical exam required by the insurer. Who can authorize that change?
column7: The insurer determines insurability and can change its own requirements. Collecting an application or payment does not give the agent that authority.

column2: An insurer's policy wording has two reasonable interpretations. Which reading does a Texas court favor?
column5: The one giving the smaller payout
column6: The one the agent used most often
column7: An ambiguity in insurance language drafted by the insurer is construed in the insured's favor. A disagreement alone does not make otherwise clear wording ambiguous.

column2: A term policy pays its full benefit after one premium if a covered death occurs. Which characteristic explains this?
column7: The value exchanged can differ greatly because the timing of death is uncertain. An adhesion contract describes who sets the wording.

column2: What makes an ordinary life policy a unilateral contract once the owner has paid the premium?
column4: Only the policy owner can cancel
column5: Only the agent can change the coverage
column6: Only the insured can choose a beneficiary
column7: The insurer must honor its promise when the policy conditions are satisfied. The owner can let the policy lapse rather than pay future premiums.

column2: A signer cannot understand what buying a policy means. Which contract requirement is in question?
column7: Capacity concerns the person's ability to understand the transaction and its consequences when signing. It is distinct from whether the premium was paid.

column2: Which payment supplies the applicant's consideration in an ordinary life insurance contract?
column6: Benefit paid on a covered death
column7: The premium is the value the applicant gives in exchange for the insurer's contractual promise. An agent's commission compensates the agent for the sale.

column2: Ruth applies at a specified premium. The insurer proposes a higher one. What has it made?
column7: A proposal at a different price changes a material term. Ruth must accept the revised offer before it forms a contract on those terms.

column2: An underwriter questions whether an applicant's income supports the requested face amount. What is being evaluated?
column7: Financial underwriting considers whether the requested amount fits the applicant's circumstances. Passing a medical exam does not by itself justify the size of the proposed policy.

column2: Nora owns a policy on her wife, Gail. Their son Ben pays premiums and their daughter Ivy is beneficiary. Who may take a policy loan?
column7: The power to borrow against available cash value belongs to the policy owner. Paying premiums or being named to receive the death benefit gives no independent borrowing right.

column2: Lee sells his entire policy in a life settlement. Who pays future premiums?
column7: The purchaser takes over the policy, pays the remaining premiums and receives the death benefit when Lee dies.

column2: Which change tends to raise a life settlement offer when the death benefit stays fixed?
column7: A shorter life expectancy brings the expected payout closer and reduces the number of premiums the purchaser expects to pay.

column2: What distinguishes contributory group life coverage from noncontributory coverage at the same workplace?
column3: Employees pay part of the premium
column7: Contributory coverage requires an employee payment toward the premium. The employer pays the whole premium for noncontributory coverage.

column2: Leah resigns before her 401(k) employer match vests. Which funds does she still own?
column7: Employees immediately own all amounts they defer from their own pay. A vesting schedule can apply separately to employer contributions.

column2: A pension formula favors highly compensated employees. Which qualification requirement addresses that practice?
column7: Federal qualification rules restrict how a plan may favor highly compensated employees in its benefits or contributions. Vesting determines when employees own their benefits.

column2: What backs an executive's benefits under an unfunded nonqualified deferred compensation plan?
column7: The employer owes the promised payment. Any assets it earmarks remain exposed to the claims of its general creditors.

column2: Which figure reduces the additional life coverage a family needs in a needs analysis?
column6: Income the family needs to replace
column7: Existing life insurance helps meet the family's needs. Debts, education expenses and lost income increase the amount the family must cover.

column2: A manufacturer needs cash to recruit and train a successor if its lead engineer dies. Which coverage fits?
column7: Key person coverage pays the business when the insured employee dies. The company can use the proceeds to replace the employee and keep operating.

column2: Two shareholders fund a cross-purchase agreement with life insurance. Who owns the policy covering each shareholder?
column7: Each shareholder owns coverage on the other and receives funds to buy the deceased shareholder's interest. In a stock redemption, the corporation buys the shares.

column2: A corporation funds a stock redemption agreement with life insurance. How will it use the proceeds?
column3: Buy back the deceased owner's shares
column4: Pay the surviving owners a dividend
column6: Repay the surviving owners' stock loans
column7: In a redemption, the business purchases the deceased owner's shares from the estate. The life policy gives the business funds for that purchase.

column2: Which unmarried 18-year-old can continue Social Security child survivor benefits based on school attendance alone?
column7: The student provision covers full-time attendance at the elementary or secondary level. Full-time college enrollment alone does not qualify.

column2: Social Security quotes a widow $1,800 for retirement and $2,200 for survivor benefits. What's her maximum monthly payment?
column7: She can receive the higher survivor amount. Social Security does not add the two full benefits together.

column2: Owen surrenders his life policy for $27,000. His tax basis is $20,000. How much is taxable?
column7: A full surrender produces taxable income to the extent that the proceeds exceed the owner's investment in the policy. The gain is $27,000 minus $20,000.

column2: How does federal tax law treat a non-MEC life policy's cash dividend below the owner's remaining basis?
column7: An ordinary policy dividend returns part of the premiums the owner paid and reduces the remaining basis. Once cumulative dividends exceed that investment, the excess is taxable.

column2: An employer fully funds group term life above the federal exclusion. What enters the employee's wages?
column6: Full death benefit on the employee
column7: The IRS uses a table to value the coverage above the exclusion. The employee reports that cost even though no death benefit has been paid.

column2: Which federal tax test determines whether excess premiums make a new life policy a modified endowment contract?
column7: The seven-pay test compares cumulative payments with the permitted total through that point in the first seven contract years. A new life policy that fails the test becomes a modified endowment contract.

column2: A modified endowment contract has $9,000 of gain. How much of a $6,000 withdrawal is taxable income?
column7: Withdrawals from a modified endowment contract come from earnings first for tax purposes. The $9,000 of gain covers the entire $6,000 withdrawal.

column2: Which expense measures the value of a stay-at-home parent's daily work when estimating life insurance needs?
column7: A survivor may need to pay someone to provide the care the parent supplied. The mortgage and college tuition are separate household needs.

column2: Whose consent does the governor need to appoint the Texas commissioner of insurance?
column7: The governor appoints the commissioner with the state Senate's advice and consent.

column2: An agent holds a carrier's premium ledgers. When may a TDI examiner inspect them?
column5: After a subpoena to the agent
column6: Once the carrier files a complaint
column7: An examiner can require free access to an agent's books and papers that concern the carrier's business.

column2: What is the longest ordinary interval between Texas financial examinations of a 20-year-old domestic insurer?
column7: Texas must examine an established carrier at least once every five years. The department can examine it sooner when needed.

column2: An agent gives TDI written notice that she needs longer to answer an inquiry. What extension must TDI grant?
column7: The usual response is due within 15 days of receipt. Written notice that more time is needed adds ten days to that deadline.

column2: TDI serves charges for an unfair trade practice. What must the accompanying hearing notice identify?
column7: When the department brings an unfair-practice proceeding, it must serve the charges and tell the respondent when and where the hearing will occur.

column2: A Texas agent's violation cost a customer money. Which sanction can repay the customer?
column7: The commissioner can direct a license holder to compensate a harmed Texas resident or insured for the loss. An administrative penalty is a separate sanction.

column2: A Texas insurer receives an emergency cease and desist order. When must it stop the specified conduct?
column3: As soon as the order is served
column5: Once a court affirms the order
column7: The order directs the insurer to stop the specified acts immediately. The opportunity to contest it does not give the insurer permission to continue them.

column2: One insurer formed in Oklahoma, another in Canada. How does Texas classify them by domicile, respectively?
column7: In Texas, an insurer organized under another US state's laws is foreign. One organized under another country's laws is alien.

column2: Who has voting rights at the annual meeting of a Texas mutual life insurance company?
column7: Policyholders have statutory voting rights at the annual meeting of a Texas mutual life insurer. Naming a beneficiary does not give that person the owner's vote.

column2: Which organization provides member benefits through representative lodges, operates without profit and has no capital stock?
column7: A fraternal benefit society has a lodge system and representative government, directly or through its qualifying fraternity. It exists for its members and beneficiaries.

column2: An unlicensed Dallas seller contacts an Oklahoma buyer. Which step first counts as insurance business in Texas?
column6: Sending the policy to the buyer
column7: Soliciting insurance in Texas is an insurance transaction even when the buyer is in another state. The Texas rule applies before an application or payment comes back.

column2: Tai and Ana earn fixed salaries. Tai accepts customers' applications. Ana only files accepted copies. Who qualifies for the clerical exclusion?
column7: Texas excludes qualifying salaried clerical staff who neither solicit nor accept public applications and earn no sales-based pay. Accepting the applications puts Tai outside that exclusion.

column2: A reciprocal Texas nonresident licensee wants to add a line. What must the agent hold at home?
column7: A reciprocal nonresident license cannot be used for a Texas line that the agent lacks authority to transact in the home state.

column2: Oklahoma suspends an agent's resident license. What happens to her corresponding reciprocal Texas license?
column7: Texas applies the corresponding home-state action automatically. A suspension in the resident state therefore suspends the reciprocal license.

column2: How long does a temporary Texas agent license remain valid from its date of issue?
column7: The statutory temporary license term is 180 days, measured from issuance.

column2: An agent runs a tax practice and an insurance agency. Which records must Texas agents keep separate?
column3: Insurance files from tax practice files
column4: Complaints from all other policy records
column6: Closed policy files from active ones
column7: Texas requires an agent to keep insurance records, including complaints, apart from records of another business the agent conducts. The same person may be a client of both.

column2: Dee has a Texas life license. What gives her authority to solicit for a particular insurer?
column7: Holding an agent license and being appointed by an authorized insurer are distinct requirements. The appointment authorizes the agent to act for that insurer.

column2: A second insurer appoints an agent today. When must they notify TDI of this additional appointment?
column3: Within 30 days of its effective date
column4: Before the agent takes any application
column5: Within 15 days of the first commission
column6: At the agent's next license renewal
column7: The agent and additional insurer must notify TDI no later than 30 days after the appointment takes effect. The agent may act for the insurer before TDI receives that notice.

column2: A Texas life agent has eight classroom-equivalent credits. How many more must use that format or a classroom?
column7: At least half of the 24 required hours must use a classroom or approved equivalent. Twelve such hours are needed, so eight already earned leave four.

column2: An agent meets renewal requirements and files on time. What authority applies while TDI processes the renewal?
column3: The existing license stays in force
column5: A temporary permit takes its place
column6: New sales require written case approval
column7: A compliant renewal filing keeps the original license effective while issuance is pending, subject to statutory nonrenewal or revocation.

column2: A federal banking regulator reprimands Leon. An Oklahoma insurance regulator fines his employer. What must Leon report as an individual Texas agent?
column7: Texas requires an agent to report administrative action taken against the agent by a state or federal financial or insurance regulator. The Oklahoma order names the employer alone.

column2: A licensed agency corporation adds a director. What is its deadline for notifying TDI?
column5: 15 days after the first board vote
column7: A licensed corporation must report a director's addition or removal within 30 days of the change.

column2: A Texas life agent's license was revoked for fraud without judicial review. When may she reapply?
column3: Five years after revocation took effect
column4: At the next biennial renewal date
column5: One year after the effective date
column7: A disciplinary revocation for fraud bars a new agent application until the fifth anniversary of its effective date when the agent does not seek judicial review. A new license is not automatic then.

column2: An agent qualifies for a medical extension of her continuing education deadline. What determines its length?
column3: Period TDI sets when granting the request
column4: Period remaining on the agent's license
column5: Recovery period stated by the physician
column6: Length of the next renewal cycle
column7: TDI sets the extension period when it grants the request. If the circumstances continue past that period, the agent may apply again.

column2: A new agent expects $120,000 in annual premiums. What minimum annual premium volume must come from uncontrolled business?
column7: An original applicant must genuinely plan to derive at least 25% of annual premiums from business outside the controlled category. A quarter of $120,000 is $30,000.

column2: An agent let her license expire four months ago. Which filing can restore her authority?
column4: Renewal application at the regular fee
column5: Late renewal with an insurer endorsement
column6: Replacement appointment from the original carrier
column7: After 90 days but before one year, Texas requires a new license application and the license fee plus an additional half-fee. Ordinary late renewal is available only during the first 90 days.

column2: A corporation seeking an agency license has one officer and two salespeople who solicit policies. Who needs individual licenses?
column7: The corporation needs at least one individually licensed officer. Each employee who acts as an agent also needs an individual license.

column2: An insurer ends an agent's appointment for cause. When must the termination details be filed with TDI?
column6: At the end of the reporting month
column7: The insurer or agent must immediately file the facts, date and cause of the termination. Texas does not give this filing the notice period used for an additional appointment.

column2: After a hearing on hazardous finances, which order can directly reduce an insurer's existing policy liabilities?
column7: Texas allows the commissioner to require reinsurance to reduce an insurer's existing and potential liabilities for policy benefits. A new-business limit controls future volume.

column2: An admitted Texas life insurer receives written notice of a claim. What is its usual deadline to acknowledge receipt?
column7: The usual acknowledgment deadline for an admitted life insurer is the 15th day after it receives notice. The 30-business-day period applies to an eligible surplus lines insurer.

column2: Which claim permits a Texas insurer to require federal tax returns for settlement without a court order?
column4: Hospital payments based on days admitted
column5: Accidental death benefits at face value
column7: Texas permits the demand for a loss of profits or income, including benefits replacing earnings. Medical expenses or a fixed death benefit do not themselves fit that exception.

column2: An insurer makes a partial payment. When may it enforce a release settling the entire claim?
column3: When the payment compromises a genuine dispute
column5: When the insurer pays the claimant directly
column6: When the claimant receives a certified check
column7: Texas makes an exception for a payment made as a compromise of a doubtful or disputed claim. An ordinary installment cannot support a full and final release.

column2: Two relatives make competing good-faith claims for the same death benefit. Which filing can resolve entitlement?
column7: The insurer may file an interpleader and deposit the benefits with the court to resolve the competing claims.

column2: A Texas insurer rejects a claim after reviewing final proof of loss. What must its notice include?
column7: The written rejection must explain why the insurer denied the claim. Simply announcing a decision does not satisfy the notice requirement.

column2: An agent says an accident rider doubles the payout even for death by illness. Which violation fits?
column7: The agent describes the rider as paying double for deaths it excludes. An untrue statement about a material policy benefit misrepresents the contract.

column2: A carrier describes a competitor's policy in a comparative ad. Who should answer questions about that description?
column7: The notice identifies the insurer whose policy is described, explains that it did not supply the description, and directs questions to its representative.

column2: Which offer to a prospective life insurance buyer constitutes a prohibited rebate in Texas?
column3: Repaying half the first premium from commission
column4: Applying an approved volume rate in the contract
column5: Issuing a participating contract with dividends
column6: Providing a customary low-cost promotional pen
column7: A personal refund offered to win the sale gives the buyer an off-contract premium concession. Texas permits participating policies and certain inexpensive promotional items.

column2: An industrial life policyholder pays the insurer directly for the required period. What may determine a premium allowance?
column7: An insurer may recognize savings when the holder of an industrial debit policy consistently pays its office directly. The allowance must fairly reflect the collection savings.

column2: What starts the 30-day reporting period for possible insurance fraud in Texas?
column7: The reporting duty arises when a person determines or reasonably suspects that a fraudulent insurance act occurred or is about to occur. The report goes in writing to TDI's insurance fraud unit.

column2: An agent wins a civil suit over a protected fraud report to TDI. What does Texas entitle the agent to recover?
column5: Lost commissions and a civil penalty
column7: A person who prevails in a civil action arising from a protected fraud report is entitled to attorney's fees and costs.

column2: Several agencies agree to shun a carrier's distributors to drive it from Texas. Which practice fits?
column7: The agencies act together to cut off the carrier's distribution and restrain competition. Texas prohibits such concerted refusals to deal.

column2: Trust A holds $24,000 of life proceeds and $6,000 in rent. Its trustee holds $4,000 for Trust B. How much may be pooled for A?
column7: Texas allows life proceeds to be pooled with other assets belonging to the same trust. Trust A's rent can join its proceeds, while Trust B's funds stay separate.

column2: A life insurer offers identical policies at different rates as a personal favor. Which applicants does Texas compare?
column3: Same class and equal life expectancy
column4: Same age and county of residence
column7: The Texas rule protects individuals classified alike who also have equal life expectancy. It applies to rates, benefits and other policy terms.

column2: An unlicensed florist refers three names at $15 each, plus $20 per sale. Two people buy. What may the agent pay?
column7: The three introductions account for $45 regardless of the outcome. An unlicensed referrer who simply passes along names cannot collect the extra $40 tied to purchases.

column2: A temporary Texas agent sells insurance covering a former employer. How far back does the commission restriction reach?
column7: The restriction covers a current employer and anyone who employed the agent within the preceding six months.

column2: Which event can activate the Texas Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Association's protection for covered benefits?
column4: Downgrade of a carrier's credit rating
column5: Payment default by the writing agency
column6: Investment loss in an owner's subaccount
column7: The association protects eligible people against unpaid covered obligations when the issuing member insurer is impaired or insolvent. Statutory coverage limits apply.

column2: An insolvent insurer's home state protects a Texas resident's policy. What does the Texas guaranty association contribute?
column5: Benefits above the home state's limit
column6: A refund of the first premium
column7: Texas excludes coverage when the insurer is domiciled elsewhere and that jurisdiction provides guaranty protection to the Texas resident.

column2: Which step must a member insurer postpone until a Texas policyholder receives the approved guaranty association summary?
column7: A Texas member insurer must provide the summary before it delivers a covered policy. The insurer must also make the summary available on request.

column2: Texas last examined an insurer in March 2025. In September 2026, how far back must its complaint record extend?
column7: The insurer must maintain its complaint record for the shorter of three years or the time since the last department examination. From March 2025 to September 2026 is 18 months.

column2: Which illustration gives a Texas whole life owner fresh projections five years after issue?
column7: An in-force illustration projects values for a policy that has already been in effect for at least a year. The original sales illustration used assumptions from the time of sale.

column2: An agent takes an annuity application in person. When are the required Texas buyer's guide and disclosure due?
column3: By the time the buyer applies
column4: When the insurer approves the risk
column7: When the annuity disclosure rules apply to a face-to-face sale, the buyer must receive both documents by the time of application.

column2: A nonaccredited buyer returns a Texas variable annuity during its free look. Surrender value is $9,600 after $180 in fees. What's refunded?
column7: Texas adds back fees and charges to the cash surrender value of an individually solicited variable annuity. Here the buyer receives $9,600 plus $180.

column2: Who must sign the receipt when a Texas life agent collects a premium under the policy's payment provision?
column3: Company officer designated in the policy
column7: Premiums are payable in advance at the insurer's home office or to its agent. For payment to the agent, the receipt must carry the signature of at least one officer designated in the policy.

column2: How far may a new Texas life policy be backdated from application to obtain a younger rating age?
column7: Texas bars backdating by more than six months to obtain a younger insurance age on an original application. A separate rule governs exchanges and conversions.

column2: When can unpaid loan principal and interest alone void a Texas whole life policy?
column3: When their total reaches the cash value
column4: When the owner misses an interest payment
column5: When the balance exceeds one annual premium
column6: When interest first exceeds the principal
column7: The debt must equal or exceed the policy's cash value before failure to repay the loan or interest can void coverage.

column2: Which proof starts the settlement period in a Texas ordinary life policy's required death claim provision?
column3: Death and the claimant's right to payment
column4: Death and the insured's premium history
column5: Funeral costs and the executor's identity
column6: Probate filing and the estate's net value
column7: The two-month period in the required policy provision runs from receipt of proof of death and proof that the claimant is entitled to the proceeds.

column2: After two years in force during the insured's lifetime, which Texas life policy restriction can still support a contest?
column7: Texas permits a continuing exception for violations of policy conditions concerning wartime military or naval service. Nonpayment of premiums is a separate exception.

column2: An owner assigns annuity benefits after the state files a child support lien notice. What remains secured?
column4: Arrears fixed on the original filing date
column7: The lien follows the assigned benefits. It secures arrears under the underlying support order, including arrears that accrue after assignment.

column2: Nora could convert $80,000 of Texas term coverage before taking a $15,000 accelerated benefit. How much remains convertible?
column7: Texas deducts the acceleration from both the death benefit and the amount otherwise available for conversion. Subtracting $15,000 leaves $65,000.

column2: A Texas group life policy permits assignments. Which proposed recipient is barred by statute?
column7: Texas allows an insured person to assign group life rights outright or as collateral under the policy's terms. The insured's employer is excluded as a recipient.

column2: Rosa dies during her workplace life conversion period before applying. How is the convertible amount paid?
column3: As a claim under the group policy
column4: As proceeds of a new individual policy
column5: As a refund of her group premiums
column6: After her estate pays the first premium
column7: The group insurer pays the amount Rosa was entitled to convert, even if she had neither applied nor paid a first individual premium.

column2: An employer ends its Texas group life policy. What minimum coverage history gives an employee a statutory conversion right?
column7: When the group policy ends, the employee must have been insured under it for at least five years. A different rule applies when an individual employee leaves a continuing plan.

column2: An employee dies while her children have dependent coverage under her Texas group life plan. What determines whether that coverage continues?
column7: Texas allows the group policy to continue some or all of the family's coverage after the insured employee dies. Whether it does so depends on the policy.

column2: An employer pays the full group life premium. Which eligible employees may the insurer exclude?
column3: Employees with unsatisfactory evidence of insurability
column4: Employees who bought individual coverage elsewhere
column5: Employees with outstanding loans on other policies
column6: Employees who did not elect payroll deductions
column7: When employees pay none of the premiums, Texas requires coverage of all eligible employees or all except those whose individual evidence of insurability is unsatisfactory.

column2: A five-year car loan has equal installments, $6,400 scheduled unpaid and $5,900 actually owed. What's the Texas credit life coverage ceiling?
column7: For substantially equal installments, Texas caps credit life coverage at the greater of the scheduled and actual unpaid balances. The scheduled balance is higher here.

column2: A bank sells an insured auto loan to a credit union. Who notifies the credit life insurer of early payoff?
column7: The holder of the debt instrument at payoff must notify the insurer of the early termination, allowing the insurer to calculate any unearned premium refund.

column2: A May 20 car loan predates the June 1 group credit life policy. Its borrower enrolls June 8. When does coverage start?
column7: For a debt already outstanding when the group policy starts, coverage begins on the later of the policy effective date and the borrower's enrollment.

column2: A buyer borrows against whole life coverage to pay another policy's first premium. How does Texas classify this?
column7: Texas treats using an existing policy's loan value for even part of the new premium as a financed purchase. The original policy can remain in force.

column2: A Texas replacement notice is presented and signed electronically. Who must mail the applicant a copy?
column4: Agent who explained the proposed replacement
column5: Company whose policy will be surrendered
column6: Custodian of the applicant's electronic records
column7: The insurer must mail a copy by the third business day after it receives the application. For a paper notice, the agent leaves it with the applicant.

column2: A replacing insurer discovers a replacement omitted from an agent's application. When must it notify the affected insurer?
column3: Within five business days of discovery
column4: Within five calendar days of delivery
column5: Within ten business days of the sale
column6: Within thirty days of the first premium
column7: When the application omits the replacement, the five-business-day period starts when the insurer identifies it. When the completed application discloses replacement, receipt starts the period.

column2: A whole life owner makes no nonforfeiture election after a premium default. Which benefit takes effect under Texas law?
column3: Paid-up benefit specified in the policy
column4: Cash surrender value paid to the owner
column5: Return of the last annual premium
column6: Paid-up option with the largest death benefit
column7: The policy identifies the paid-up benefit that takes effect by default. The owner can elect another available option within 60 days after the missed premium's due date.

column2: Under a Texas life policy, what event starts the minimum two-year period allowed for filing suit?
column3: Accrual of the cause of action
column7: Texas bars a policy from shortening the time to sue to less than two years after the cause of action accrues. That is the point when the legal claim arises.
